source_review.notes: Reviewed current ISO C++ queue/adaptor clauses, Rust VecDeque, Java SE 25 Queue/BlockingQueue/ArrayBlockingQueue, current Python deque/queue documentation, the primary Michael-Scott PODC queue paper, and the Go channel specification. All ten final destinations returned HTTP 200.

evidence: Checked front-to-back Q, append-back/remove-front transitions, accepted admission, depth/capacity, head/tail, in-flight, and lifecycle terminology.
Separated FIFO element order from arrival, waiter wakeup, scheduling, service completion, fairness, priority, and durable delivery.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Core link/index cost is distinguished from allocation, wait, scheduling, retry, reclamation, and persistence.

evidence: Replayed capacity-three trace: offer A/B, poll A, offer C/D, reject E, then poll B/C/D and observe underflow.
Confirmed total removal order A,B,C,D, size returns zero, both head and tail clear, and invariant remains true.
Checked example capacities/sizes, including linked singleton transition and 10 times 20 MB exceeding a 64 MB budget.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Finite values validate the examples, not blocking or concurrent histories.

evidence: Re-derived FIFO by induction over accepted enqueue operations followed by remove-front transitions.
Checked linked head/tail constant link work and naive array front erasure linear movement.
Checked head-offset amortized compaction and ring/segmented alternatives are presented with their additional assumptions rather than universal bounds.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Concurrent FIFO is scoped to a legal real-time-respecting linearization, not call-start or completion order.

evidence: Reviewed empty, singleton, capacity zero, exact full, just-over-full, item/byte overflow, large payload, repeated/null-like values, allocation/return failure, and bulk partial acceptance.

Reviewed reject/block/timeout/drop/coalesce/spill, cancelled wait, timeout-publication race, multiple consumers, in-flight work, poison pills, producer crash, consumer abandonment, close-buffered, and close-drained.
Reviewed retained array prefixes, stale iterators, forced node reuse, ABA, stalled reclamation, overload, malicious sizes, and high-stakes delivery boundaries.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Dropping/coalescing policies are explicitly treated as different observable semantics.

evidence: Checked linked head reaches exactly size live nodes, last equals tail, tail.next terminates, and empty iff both endpoints are null.
Checked successful offer publishes one node, full rejection has no effect, poll removes one head, and singleton poll clears tail.
Checked capacity bounds and complete return to empty after the finite trace.
invariant_checking.notes: Python's managed nodes do not establish manual reclamation safety.

evidence: Reviewed FIFO induction for successful admissions and explicit exclusions for cancellation/removal/failure.
Reviewed linked enqueue/dequeue transition order for construction, head/tail publication, return, and reclamation.
Reviewed bounded/lifecycle proof obligations for timeout races, wakeups, close, drain, and terminal results.
proof_review.notes: Michael-Scott and other concurrent algorithms still require implementation- and memory-model-specific proof.

evidence: Sequential FIFO and representation arguments name successful-operation and stability premises.
Fairness, backpressure, concurrent progress, durability, exactly-once, security, reliability, and deployment remain separate claims.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: The historical paper is evidence for an algorithm design, not certification of a future implementation.

evidence: The standard-library Python snippet passed exact seven-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status under recorded Python 3.14.4.
It emits evidence=finite_bounded_queue_trace, and all ten source destinations plus all local links were checked directly.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No C++/Rust/Java/Python/Go production queue, allocator failure, blocking waiter, concurrent history, reclamation, workload benchmark, durable broker, or high-stakes service was empirically evaluated.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed FIFO abstraction, empty APIs, linked/array/ring/segmented representations, accepted-history order, capacity/backpressure, blocking/timeouts, close, bulk, retention, iteration/persistence, concurrency, evidence dynamics, and alternatives.
